chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Jamilah from Mu'alla ibn Khunays said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, while I was present, about a man who married a woman on the basis of his female slave who was manumitted in part (mudabbarah), whom the woman knew and had precedence over, and he divorced her before consummating the marriage with her.
He said, 'I see that the wife is entitled to half of the service of the mudabbarah, so the wife has one day of service, and the master who manumitted her has one day of service.'
It was said to him, 'If the mudabbarah dies before the wife and the master, to whom will the inheritance belong?'
He said, 'Half of what she left belongs to the wife, and the other half belongs to her master who manumitted her.'

key_terms.مُدَبَّرَةٍ: A slave who is manumitted in part (e.g., one-third or half) upon the master's death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry of a partially manumitted slave if the husband divorces before consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the application of *ta'wil* (interpretive reasoning) by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in determining financial rights when a *mudabbar* (partially manumitted slave) is used as a dowry (*mahr*) or conditional asset. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that divorce prior to consummation entitles the wife to half the value of the dowry, here quantified as half the slave's remaining service period, while also clarifying inheritance dynamics upon the slave's death.
